name: Eco-Fascism
summary: Eco-fascism fuses environmental concern with fascist politics: it holds that a people has a mystical bond with its homeland and that ecological survival requires authoritarian rule, sharply restricted immigration and drastic cuts or racial selection in population. Its adherents blame industrial civilisation, consumerism and overpopulation for ecological decline, and many accept terror or accelerating collapse to bring about a new order.
scope: Profile of the self-described ecofascist current since the 2010s (Christchurch and El Paso manifestos, Terrorgram-style networks, Greenline Front) and its lineage as documented by scholars: Nazi blood-and-soil agrarianism (Darre), Madison Grant, Savitri Devi, Garrett Hardin's lifeboat ethics and Pentti Linkola's authoritarian deep ecology. Hardin and Linkola are precursors or heroes of the milieu and did not necessarily call themselves ecofascists. It excludes mainstream environmentalism and the pejorative use of the label against green groups. It is an unorganised milieu with no party programme, so many answers are inferred and low confidence.

missingStatements.text: Overpopulation is the main cause of environmental destruction.
missingStatements.rationale: Ecofascists name overpopulation as the central environmental threat, as did Hardin and Linkola.

missingStatements.text: A nation has a spiritual bond with its homeland and a duty to protect the land of its ancestors.
missingStatements.rationale: The mystical bond between nation and homeland is the core of blood and soil and of Zimmerman's definition.

notes: Strands differ: 'custodians' want to protect their ethnic group's homeland, 'conquerors' preserve the environment for their race's survival (Campion). Some accelerationists want the state destroyed, while authoritarian strands want a totalitarian state. Kaczynski rejected fascism and racism. Critics such as David Orton say the label is mainly a smear.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sources say nothing on health care; adherents focus on race and ecology, and a racial welfare-state view and a laissez-faire view both exist, so this is genuinely open.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is not discussed in ecofascist writing; the movement is indifferent to it and splits along nationalist-socialist versus market lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ecofascists blame industrial capitalism for ecological decline and the Nazi tradition subordinated markets to blood and soil, though little explicit economic doctrine exists.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership of utilities is not addressed; the Nazi agrarian tradition protected peasant farms rather than nationalising industry, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position on taxation; hostility to cosmopolitan elites coexists with indifference to redistribution.

unions-good.rationale: Nazi-era blood-and-soil politics replaced independent unions with state bodies, and modern ecofascists show no interest in labour organising; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Hardin and Linkola would subordinate property to ecological limits and state control of the commons, so property is not treated as near-sacred; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Ecofascism blames over-industrialisation for environmental decline, so tighter control of industrial firms follows from its core diagnosis.

cut-welfare.rationale: Hardin opposed aid abroad but welfare for the in-group is not discussed; adherents split between racial welfare nationalism and austerity.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; the ideology centres on land and race rather than workplace ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Authoritarian ecofascists accept state coercion to enforce ecological and racial goals, but surveillance specifically is inferred, and accelerationist strands distrust the state.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Hardline-style subcultures stressed purity and discipline and the Nazi tradition was moralistic; drug policy itself is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Ecofascists openly promote racial and ethnonationalist ideas and treat speech restrictions as a tool of their enemies; some regimes of theirs would censor opponents, but the statement as asked is opposed.

strong-leader.rationale: Linkola said democracy was a mistake and preferred dictatorships, and the fascist label rests on authoritarian leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Authoritarian ecofascists want a strong state to enforce ecological limits, while accelerationist strands want the state destroyed; the strands differ.

limit-guns.rationale: Attacks in the movement were committed with firearms and the subculture is armed; the position is inferred and a ruling ecofascist state would monopolise arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order, discipline and enforcement are central to fascism and Linkola's authoritarian measures; ecofascists want coercive capacity to impose their programme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The Nazi cult of peasant motherhood and the Hardline subculture's moralism point against, but sex work is not discussed; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Blood and soil prizes local rootedness, yet ecofascist programmes demand central authoritarian enforcement, so adherents are split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Ecofascist thought stresses hierarchy, purity and harsh enforcement over reform; prison policy is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Blood and soil idealised peasant families and women as bearers of strong children, and Hardline opposed abortion and contraception; modern strands also stress ethnic reproduction.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Hardline subculture called homosexuality unnatural, and the Nazi tradition was hostile; some modern strands differ, so not strong.

abortion-legal.rationale: Hardline opposed abortion and Nazi ideology promoted racial natalism, while Malthusian strands favour population limits; the typical stance is inferred and strands differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Greenline Front rejects monotheism and Savitri Devi was pagan; many ecofascists seek a nature-mystic spirituality instead of church influence.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ecofascists are racial nationalists who treat race as the basis of politics and reject remedies for historical racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Blood-and-soil thinking holds fixed natural roles for sexes and races; the position is implied by naturalism rather than argued directly.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement is defined by protecting an ethnic homeland and its culture, with a mystical bond between nation and land.

gradual-change.rationale: Many ecofascists demand radical change or accelerate societal collapse, and Linkola called for drastic measures; established institutions are distrusted.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to immigration is central: Hardin's lifeboat ethics and manifestos link immigration directly to environmental damage.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hardin called the UN a toothless tiger, and ecofascists reject globalism and global governance as a threat to the nation and its land.

free-trade.rationale: Le Pen-style green nationalism opposes free trade for economic patriotism, and ecofascists blame globalised industry for ecological harm.

nation-first.rationale: Lifeboat ethics holds rich nations should put their own survival first, and ethnic nationalism is central to the ideology.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hardin argued against rescuing the poor and nationalists reject foreign human-rights wars, so intervention is inferred to be opposed.

open-borders.rationale: Hardin held that unrestricted immigration moves people to the food and ruins rich countries, and ecofascists call immigration an environmental invasion.

limit-growth.rationale: Over-industrialisation is blamed for environmental decline and Linkola urged a return to pre-industrial limits on human life.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Ecofascists see collapse as imminent and want radical measures, but frame them as population cuts and exclusion, and some deny a climate emphasis; mainstream strand agrees.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Anti-industrial and Kaczynski-inspired strands see technology as the cause of the crisis, and Linkola wanted a return to pre-industrial life.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Le Pen's National Rally backs nuclear power while primitivist ecofascists reject industrial energy; adherents are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Many ecofascists advocate accelerating collapse and terror so that a fascist order can replace the present one.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authoritarian rule is favoured but by leaders and the racial community rather than technocrats; adherents differ.

central-planning.rationale: Totalitarian direction of life by a state is favoured by some, but economic planning is rarely specified; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic ownership forms are not a defined concern of the ideology.

land-value-tax.rationale: No ecofascist source discusses land taxation, so there is no basis for a position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; Nazi hereditary farm law protected inheritance of peasant land, but wealth taxes are not addressed.

basic-income.rationale: Hardin's lifeboat ethics rejects giving out unconditional support; inferred, as no source addresses basic income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic patriotism and opposition to free trade are documented for green-nationalist parties, though ecofascists dislike industry itself.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; opposed pulls of anti-industrialism and nationalist state direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Blood and soil elevated the independent peasant landholder, and the 1933 Reich Hereditary Farm Law protected small farms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No stated interest in abolishing money, though anti-industrial primitivist strands might; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in ecofascist writing; the ideology's economics is thin.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Nazi state organised labour under state bodies, but modern ecofascist writing does not address bargaining structures.

one-party-rule.rationale: Linkola preferred dictatorship and the fascist tradition rules through a single movement, though many modern ecofascists are decentralised accelerationists.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Fascist tradition is republican-leader based and ecofascists rarely discuss monarchy; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Linkola called democracy a mistake and preferred dictatorships; ecofascism holds ecological survival overrides majority choice.

direct-votes.rationale: Rejection of democracy extends to direct voting in general; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: A fascist order is hostile to class-based councils and to democratic bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ecofascists want ethnostates and could favour secession for their own people, yet fascists defend national unity; split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Racial and natural hierarchy is central: Madison Grant and Darré held Nordic superiority and eugenics-based rule by the fit.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ecofascists favour terror over politics, from Christchurch to Linkola's support for the Madrid bombings.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fascist tradition glorifies struggle and ecofascist strands see violence as heroic; however some stress isolation not war, and it is inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strands conflict between pagan hostility to churches and Christian-identity strands; not documented.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ecofascists tend to be pagan or anti-monotheist (Greenline Front, Savitri Devi) and base law on nature and race, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They want a strong authoritarian state; private provision of law and defence conflicts with that.

military-superiority.rationale: Nazi Lebensraum expansion involved military power, but modern ecofascists are inwardly focused; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The ideology defines the nation by ethnicity bound to its land; manifestos call for ethnic homelands.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fascism replaces class conflict with race and nation as the engine of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy by race and fitness is central, rejecting egalitarian aims.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Custodian ecofascists claim their own ethnic group's native land, but concern for non-European indigenous peoples is unstated; split.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hardin rejected obligations to the poor world; nationalists reject reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some strands want pan-European or white unity, others national separatism; unclear.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ecofascism demands sacrifice of individual interest to the land and the nation, per Zimmerman.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Zimmerman's definition says people must sacrifice their interests for the land, placing duty above individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecocentric strands (Campion's custodians, Linkola, Savitri Devi) value nature for itself and over human interests, though anthropocentric conquerors protect it for their race.

limit-population.rationale: Overpopulation is described as the main environmental threat, and Hardin and Linkola both demanded strict limits or radical reduction of human numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Over-industrialisation is blamed for ecological decline, and Linkola wanted a return to pre-industrial life.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Anti-industrial ecofascists see technological acceleration as worsening collapse, even though some accelerationists want social disruption, not technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Blood and soil and nature-mystic views favour natural purity; inferred, since transhumanist enhancement is not discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Ecofascists favour rule by human leaders and the racial community, and distrust industrial technology; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Online ecofascist networks such as Terrorgram use encrypted channels, but the ideology itself takes no stand.

restore-past-order.rationale: Blood and soil looks to a rooted pre-industrial peasant order, and Linkola wanted a return to pre-industrial life over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The ideology holds ideological commitments about race and nature above case-by-case pragmatism; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Ecofascists favour terror and direct violence over elections and engagement in politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Violent means are used to build a hierarchical order, so means do not mirror the intended society; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Linkola wanted pre-industrial life, not foraging specifically; deep-ecology strands differ, and the statement goes beyond sources.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchy and roles, such as the Nazi peasant and woman roles, are valued over abolishing specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Hardin's lifeboat ethics rejects needs-based sharing with the poor, and race-based hierarchy contradicts universal need.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-capitalist strands in some groups, but no documented economic doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fascist tradition rejects Marxist exploitation theory, though it opposes finance capital; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Fascism is by definition opposed to proletarian dictatorship and class rule, replacing it with the racial nation.

collective-farming.rationale: Nazi agrarianism valued independent peasant farmers on hereditary farms, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a documented ecofascist claim; they blame industrialism and population instead.

taxation-theft.rationale: Authoritarian state-first view rejects libertarian claims; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Zimmerman's definition requires individuals to sacrifice interests for the land, far beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ecofascism ranks the land, race and community above individuals, and denies individual rights as primary.

conscription.rationale: Totalitarian fascist states mobilise citizens for national service, and Linkola favoured authoritarian limits on life.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy is rejected, and the ideology wants binding authority, not exit options.

state-as-business.rationale: Ecofascists see the state as the guardian of land and race, not a service company.

positive-liberty.rationale: The ideology concerns collective duty over individual freedom of any kind; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Manifestos adopt Great Replacement and anti-elite conspiracy narratives that blame media and academic elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Madison Grant's Nordic racial theory, which Nazis adopted, and Darré's eugenics hold ability is racially inherited; Hardin has been called a white nationalist.

organic-representation.rationale: Blood and soil sought organic community structures such as peasantry and families, but sources do not detail representation; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Zimmerman defines ecofascism as totalitarian government demanding sacrifice for the land, so the state directs life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ecofascists want radical renewal of the racial nation and a return to soil; collapse is expected to clear the way for a new order.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nazi blood and soil fed Lebensraum, but modern custodian ecofascists want to protect existing homelands; strands differ.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Leader oaths exist in fascist tradition, but feudal lord-follower rule is not specifically held.

bound-labor.rationale: Hereditary farms tied peasants to land in the Nazi law but with ownership not serfdom; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nazi and ecofascist thought distrusts universal science in some strands while using eugenic science in others; no clear stance.

universal-morality.rationale: Ecofascism assigns rights by race and land and rejects universal moral equality.

single-common-good.rationale: Fascist tradition posits one organic national good above group interests; the land and race come first.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Antisemitic currents dominate, though a few ethnostate advocates admire ethnic homelands; stance mostly inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed; ethnic homeland logic suggests support for kin return but sources do not say.

revive-national-language.rationale: Sources do not discuss language revival; ethnonationalism might favour it but the milieu says nothing specific.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic control by workers conflicts with authoritarian hierarchy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not addressed in ecofascist sources, so no position is documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of the ideology, and nothing in the sources implies a stance on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Authoritarian ecofascists deny that freedom depends on markets, and Linkola preferred dictatorship; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not clearly addressed; the movement uses coercion and also moral heroism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Ecofascism seeks ethnic homelands governing themselves, though universalism for all nations is not articulated.

force-without-un.rationale: Nationalists reject UN authority over their state, as Hardin called the UN a toothless tiger; use of force abroad itself is inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Ecofascism relies on mystical bonds to the land and emotion, though it also draws on scientific racism; mixed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Hardin and nationalist ecofascists oppose extending resources to outsiders and immigrants, reserving them for the in-group.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditions are not discussed; racial welfare nationalists might agree, but the sources are silent.

class-collaboration.rationale: Fascism replaces class struggle with national solidarity, and blood and soil unified farmers and nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage and homeland preservation is valued, though anti-modern strands care little for institutions; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Western ethnonationalists do not align with the Global South, which they blame for population growth.

workers-nation.rationale: Fascism sees workers as part of the nation rather than an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Blood and soil idealised peasant women as mothers and sturdy workers, and Hardline opposed abortion and homosexuality.

ban-interest.rationale: Nazi rhetoric attacked interest slavery but ecofascism sources are silent.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The sources describe separate ethnic homelands rather than segregation laws within one state.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Fascism denies the class-instrument theory of the state; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposition to industrial extraction is central; they blame industrialisation for ecological decline.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Ecofascists want immigration halted and see immigrants as an invasion, not as candidates for assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The Great Replacement conspiracy appears in several ecofascist manifestos including Christchurch.

proportional-representation.rationale: Democratic procedure is rejected, so electoral design is not a priority; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Not documented; Nazi expansion had a mission, but modern ecofascism is insular.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Blood and soil celebrated natural sex roles and does not recognise structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ecofascists treat political and elite classes as enabling replacement and ecological ruin.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Darré proposed a systematic eugenics breeding programme, and Grant and Hardin traditions favoured selective population control.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Ecofascists would not accept being held accountable for violence on their own side; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They demand totalitarian or dictatorial states enforcing ecological limits, not limited government.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial purity is central to Grant's and Darré's thought, and Christchurch-type manifestos defend ethnic separation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ecofascism ranks peoples by race and valued land over individuals, as in the Zimmerman and Campion definitions.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist doctrinal question not addressed; fascism rejects internationalism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not documented; ethnonationalists reject framing their states as colonial.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal-law questions are not discussed in ecofascist sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not addressed; hostility to Islam and monotheism pulls in different directions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Some strands such as Savitri Devi and the Finnish Blue-and-Black Movement oppose ritual slaughter and animal exploitation, yet cattle bans are not discussed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sources do not address school religion, and pagan and Christian-identity strands would answer differently.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is an internal Marxist-Leninist debate that ecofascist sources do not touch.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Linkola called democracy a mistake and favoured dictatorship, implying legitimacy does not depend on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed beyond opposition to free trade.

population-transfer.rationale: Ecofascists advocate expelling or excluding racial outgroups, up to genocide in extreme versions, to protect the homeland.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The sources describe ecofascist support for terror and forced population control, and Linkola backed bombings; the libertarian axiom is not discussed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist lineage runs through Grant and Darré, though ecofascists view modernity as decline, not progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Would be on the receiving end; favours authoritarian rule though not a ban on rivals as stated.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty theory is foreign; domination by outgroups matters more.

separated-powers.rationale: Linkola preferred dictatorship over checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Accelerationist cells and the idea of an enlightened vanguard recur, but without Marxist class framing.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Hardin explicitly opposed giving priority to the poor, comparing them to people swimming around a full lifeboat.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are not addressed in ecofascist sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Nazi-style state suppressed strikes; inferred for modern strands.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Hardin argued poor nations' population growth widens the gap and aid worsens it, and ecofascists see overpopulation as the main problem.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ecofascists defend ethnic homogeneity and treat immigration as damaging to cohesion and ecology.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejects democratic methods in favour of strong leadership.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian ecofascists justify extraordinary measures against internal enemies and for ecological crisis.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not discussed; the ideology has no documented economic programme on this.

party-controls-media.rationale: Totalitarian structures control media in Zimmerman's picture, but modern groups more often rail against media; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Fascist tradition includes party armies, but this specific institutional question is not documented.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Restrictive nationalists and Hardin want strict immigration control, and many want no naturalisation of outsiders.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not discussed, and the ideology rejects representative democracy generally.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fascist movements demand discipline, but sources do not address party rules in this movement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Rejection of supranational bodies and globalism is explicit; Hardin disdained the UN.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Linkola preferred dictatorship, which places command in the ruler.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed in ecofascist sources, which are often pagan or secular.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ecofascist strands are often pagan or anti-monotheist and put race and land over clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalists support their nation in war, though some accelerationists want the system to fall.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi culture policy censored degenerate art, but ecofascist writing does not address it; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Dictatorial preference implies no limits on rule; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Democratic accountability devices are not a concern under dictatorship preference.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Isolationist nationalism and lifeboat ethics suggest disengagement, but it is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in the sources on ecofascism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed ecofascist groups and mass shooters celebrate private arms, but the call for armed citizenry replacing the army is inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Blood and soil held the countryside as the organic racial community while cities were corrupt asphalt culture.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Blood-and-soil politics seeks to unite a people on its land, and Nazi expansion pursued this, but modern ecofascist sources do not discuss border disputes.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elite conspiracy attitudes suggest it; not documented specifically.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Grant's Nordic superiority and the ecofascist race hierarchy deny that cultures and races are merely different.

death-penalty.rationale: Authoritarian and violent strands favour harsh punishment and Linkola advocated killing, so execution is inferred as supported.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality curricula conflict with blood and soil gender roles; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Ecofascists favour pagan or nature-mystic views and draw on biology for race; creationism is not a documented concern.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moralistic purity themes in Nazi and Hardline culture; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Blood and soil ties nationality to descent, as the Nazi Hereditary Farm Law did for farming; citizenship law is not discussed directly.

minority-language-support.rationale: Ethnonationalists favour a single national culture; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Hostile to minority religions and immigrants; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The ideology demands conformity to the community and land; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Hardin opposed aid, so cancelling poor-country debt is likely rejected, but debt is unaddressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: An anti-colonial debate that ecofascist sources do not engage with.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Opposes democratic institution building; inferred from dictatorship preference.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarians would restrict freedoms but for ecological limits, not growth, which they oppose.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Hardin's lifeboat ethics argues rich countries have no duty to aid the world's poor and that aid worsens population growth.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; Le Pen backs nuclear power but defence policy is not documented for ecofascists.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Dictatorship preference rejects elections broadly, but plebiscitary leaders exist in fascism; not documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in ecofascist writing, so no position is documented.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Blood-and-soil attachment to the homeland implies refusing to surrender it; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Zimmerman's definition has individuals sacrificing their interests for the land, so property is subordinate to the collective good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist classification debate not addressed in ecofascist sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Ecofascists hold ecological limits take priority and that collapse is near, supporting early action.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists distrust alliances but not documented.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International-law questions on annexation are not addressed in ecofascist sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nazi state subordinated churches, but the statement is not documented for modern ecofascism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A dictator embodies the movement, not a neutral symbol; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources are silent; ecofascists favour ethnic separatism for their own people but fascist tradition defends national unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-administrative-region arrangements are not discussed in ecofascist sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Fascist leader cult exists, but divine descent is not claimed; pagan strands may sacralise nature, not rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income-tax design is not discussed by the sources on ecofascism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Grant's and Darré's racial theories hold that character and ability derive from innate racial stock, not circumstance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Linkola preferred dictatorship, which places the ruler above ordinary legal limits.

space-expansion.rationale: Anti-industrial and anti-technology ecofascists reject space expansion as more of the same overreach.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Dictatorship preference rejects balanced constitutions; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: The fascist tradition includes leader veneration, and Tarrant-style manifestos honour heroic figures; not a core ecofascist doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed; traditional-family views might imply a maternal presumption but no source says so.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist debate about socialist society that ecofascists do not engage with.

land-redistribution.rationale: Nazi policy preserved hereditary farms, not redistribution; adherents otherwise silent.

refugee-return.rationale: Ecofascists oppose migrants and favour exclusion and expulsion; refugees returning to homes in others' territory is not endorsed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Lebensraum and blood-and-soil politics asserted claims for ethnic Germans abroad; modern strands vary.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Often anti-monotheist, so religious enforcement is not held; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed, and nationalists oppose Islamic practices, though not by mandating dress.

common-currency.rationale: Opposes supranational integration such as the EU and its currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: White or Nordic unity appears in some manifestos, though ethnonationalists also stress separate homelands.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural institutions are not discussed; ethnonationalism points against, but sources are silent.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The ideology rejects minority claims inside its own nation; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fascism and blood-and-soil thought see race and nation, not economic relations, as the driver of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; anti-elite sentiment and economic nationalism pull in opposite directions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The majority concept is not central; they favour authoritarian rule, not majoritarian courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Blood and soil gender roles oppose parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is consistent with opposition to free trade and global industry, and Nazi blood-and-soil rhetoric valued self-sufficiency.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Opposes international trade agreements as such; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work incentives are not discussed in the sources on ecofascism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Accelerationist ecofascists believe small armed attacks can precipitate collapse and a new order.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary landholding and bloodline were valued by Darré's thinking.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural preservation and nationalism favour history centred on the in-group.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hardin rejected involvement with poor countries; ecofascists want separation, not tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism and the Nazi education tradition promote loyalty and national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Ecofascists reject race-based remedies, though for racial reasons rather than colour-blindness.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The ideology predicts collapse of industrial society; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed, and modern ecofascists are mostly insular.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarkic nationalists want separation from global trade; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that ecofascist sources do not address.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Racial separatists reject anti-discrimination law; not discussed directly in sources.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights limiting authority conflict with totalitarian ecological rule.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaty validity is not addressed in ecofascist sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Linkola rejected democracy for dictatorship, so choosing rulers by election is disfavoured, though succession rules are not specified.

minority-veto.rationale: The ideology demands individual sacrifice to the whole; minority vetoes are not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed for a ruler of their own movement.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Linkola held democracy a mistake, so parliament-supreme rule is opposed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Savitri Devi combined Nazism with animal rights and vegetarianism, and the Blue-and-Black Movement opposes fur farming and ritual slaughter.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Strands conflict: some demand vegetarianism and animal rights, while others hunt and farm.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not documented; racial hierarchy implies duty to the in-group only.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ecofascists urge activism and violence, though Kaczynski-style primitivist strands withdraw.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anti-modern critique of consumer society is common; the specific claim is inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not used in ecofascist sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Hardin held poor nations are poor due to population growth, not extraction by rich nations.

native-born-offices.rationale: Ethnic nationalism reserves political authority for the native in-group.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist-party debate that ecofascism sources do not engage with.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Hardin argued that aid removes incentives and should be refused, leaving poor nations to rely on themselves.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nazi Germany pursued lost territory, but modern ecofascists do not discuss it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Custodian ecofascists claim their own native land but do not address the point generally.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Ecofascists identify with fascism; constitutional anti-fascism is not discussed but runs directly against them.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They deny equivalence to fascism; Kaczynski called ecofascism a leftist aberration, so stances vary.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not directly addressed; far-right sympathies suggest denial, but it is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Traditional gender views and manosphere overlap in far-right spaces; not documented in sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; traditional gender views and far-right male-grievance themes do not clearly decide it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rejection of universalism and equal cultures implies institutions suit particular peoples, as Hardin's lifeboat logic and race thought indicate.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authoritarian preferences suggest it; not documented.

paid-care-work.rationale: Blood and soil celebrated unpaid peasant motherhood as natural duty; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Traditional family and rooted community values; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not addressed in ecofascist sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic patriotism opposes foreign ownership, as in Le Pen's platform.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Blood and soil idealised the stable peasant family, so easier divorce is likely disfavoured, but no source states a divorce position.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Democratic recall mechanisms conflict with dictatorship.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is held in trust for the people and race under blood and soil, not as a commodity, though inheritance of farms was protected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Rule by dictatorship rejects parliamentary control; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Ethnonationalism favours one national language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Blood and soil tie land to the people, and the Nazi farm law limited farmland to people of German blood.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Ecofascists reject race-based remedies and see unequal outcomes as natural.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Ecofascists blame consumption and industrialism, and Linkola said boastful consumption must be crushed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Isolationist lifeboat ethics suggests avoiding foreign entanglements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intra-bloc military intervention is a Cold War question that ecofascists do not discuss.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-globalist and anti-elite narratives target corporate power, and they blame over-industrialisation.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nationalists oppose foreign influence on media and civil society, as in the Great Replacement framing.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Overpopulation is the core worry, so rewarding births is mostly opposed; but ethnic natalism in the Nazi lineage supports it for the in-group; mixed lean no.

residents-only-property.rationale: Blood-and-soil localism restricts land ownership to the rooted community.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is not discussed; the sources give no basis for a position.

democratic-peace.rationale: Linkola held democracy a mistake, so spreading it is not a goal.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Terror strands reject lawfulness, while authoritarian strands demand obedience.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in ecofascist sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Manifestos adopt the Great Replacement conspiracy, and antisemitic narratives are widespread in the milieu.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditional family ideals under blood and soil suggest opposition, though no source discusses legal marriage.

local-production.rationale: Blood and soil prizes rooted agrarian life, and anti-industrial ecofascists favour local production over global trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: Contemporary ecofascist movements organise via small leaderless cells and online networks like Terrorgram.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Opposition to supranational bodies and Hardin's lifeboat view put national sovereignty above international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Ethnic nation, not religion, defines the community, and Greenline Front rejects monotheism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nationalists reject subordination of their nation to others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Local rooted community preference suggests retaining revenue; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist formulation that ecofascist sources do not take a position on.

defeat-communism.rationale: Fascism defined itself against communism, but modern ecofascists rarely talk of it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Savitri Devi and others hold a mystic view of nature, so religion is not dismissed, though monotheism is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Industrial capitalism is seen as the cause of ecological disaster, not as progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Blood and soil assigned natural roles to women and does not demand equality.

socialized-care.rationale: Family and peasant motherhood idealised, so care stays private.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Nazi-era linguistic nationalism; for modern ecofascists inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed; ethnonationalism points against indigenous deals but nothing says so.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ecofascists favour rooted communities but under authority, and cooperatives are not a feature.

majority-settlement.rationale: Lebensraum policies settled Germans in conquered lands; modern strands are separatist, so low.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-position stance: rejects both liberal industrial capitalism and Marxism, in line with blood and soil.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Mystical bond between nation and homeland gives ancestral claims weight.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Neo-Nazi strands often deny it, while others do not discuss it, so the typical stance is split.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Hardline called homosexuality unnatural, but many modern ecofascists do not call for criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Totalitarian and dictatorial ecofascism would suppress opposition to enforce ecological order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Pagan and anti-monotheist leanings oppose blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Isolationist lifeboat logic rejects overseas rule; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The statement concerns a Muslim religious duty that ecofascists never address; their hostility to Muslim immigration is a different question, so this is a guess.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Manifestos target Muslim immigration, and a ruler-removal doctrine of political Islam is alien to a race- and land-based ideology.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Linkola and others reject democracy in favour of dictatorship; participatory democracy is not discussed by name.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Ecofascists reject intersectional analysis and treat race as the basis of group interests.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Hardline opposed homosexuality as deviant and blood and soil assumes fixed sex roles.

assisted-dying.rationale: Linkola-type population thinking is harsh on life, but sources do not address assisted dying; split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Some call themselves beyond left and right, and Nils Gilman's avocado image suggests mixed green-brown positions; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-industrial critique overlaps, but the Marxist concept is not used.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Ecofascist manifestos target Muslim immigrants as invaders, and the milieu holds Islam alien to European or Western culture.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from nature, race and land in the ideology, though Christian-identity strands exist.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Opposition to Muslim immigration suggests support, but it is inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not a concern of the ideology; no source addresses workplace harassment rules.

social-market-economy.rationale: The ideology criticises industrial capitalism and does not endorse its softened form.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The fascist tradition the movement draws on glorifies military strength; abolishing armies is not discussed.

rich-first.rationale: Hardin's logic implies rich nations protect themselves first, while the statement is about step-by-step development, which he doubted.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Lifeboat isolationism and nationalism favour staying out of rival blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Bloodline matters but fascist leaders are not usually hereditary; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit reform is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Nationalists reject outside creditors dictating policy; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Race, not wealth, is the voting criterion for racial separatists.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Blood and soil celebrated male-led natural hierarchy and did not seek to end domination of women.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Lukacsian concept that ecofascist sources do not use.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not an ecofascist concern as such, though media distrust is common.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Dictatorship preference and terrorism imply rule outside fixed laws; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ecofascists want ethnically separate homelands, which ties political membership to race; voting rules are not discussed directly.

online-participation.rationale: Democratic participation is rejected, even if the milieu organises online.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Race, not religion, is the marriage concern of ecofascists.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Antisemitic and anti-immigrant tendencies make it plausible, but it is not documented as a tactic.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Linkola rejected democracy, so deliberative citizen bodies are disfavoured; the specific question is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not addressed; the milieu includes pagans, Christian-identity and anti-monotheist currents.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Liberty is not a core value; anti-elite views exist but are not framed by wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Hardline hostility to homosexuality and fascist military culture; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Pagan and nature-spiritual strands want spiritual renewal, not atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ecofascists favour authoritarian coercion and enforcement; the sources do not discuss police abolition as such.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ethnonationalists want separation or exclusion rather than sharing power with other communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Hardin opposed aid, but domestic charity versus state is not addressed.

term-limits.rationale: Dictatorship preference opposes limits on leaders; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a form of democratic participation, which Linkola called a mistake.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Ecofascists see ecological collapse as the existential threat, but frame it around nation and race, not humanity.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed in ecofascist sources, and strands differ on religion itself.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Blood and soil idealised male-headed peasant households; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ecofascists oppose immigration and exclude outsiders from the national community; local voting rights are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Housing market regulation is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Nazi tradition built uniformed youth organisations for national service, and fascist movements imitate them.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; strands split on nuclear energy and arms.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Nationalist sovereignty and lifeboat isolationism suggest it; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Holocaust denial and genocide advocacy in the milieu make recognition unlikely.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Blood and soil prized peasant labour over finance, though economic doctrine is thin.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Violence is central to the ideology as the sources describe it; absolute pacifism is not discussed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Blood and soil holds an unbroken bond of blood and soil from ancient Nordic origins to the present.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Fixed natural sexes underpin blood and soil roles.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The ideology assumes natural categories of men and women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Christchurch and El Paso attackers are venerated as saints in the milieu such as Terrorgram, and fascism honours fallen heroes.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Blood and soil carries a mystical bond of land and people, and Savitri Devi cast Nazism in religious terms.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora relations are not addressed in sources on ecofascism.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not documented; some strands stress cultural-spiritual renewal and others state-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Not a concern; pagan strands may use goddess imagery, but sources are silent.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnonationalism wants national resources controlled by the native in-group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ethnic homeland logic favours unifying a people, but not documented.

independent-unions.rationale: Nazi state absorbed unions; modern strands do not address them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rejects socialist-revolution definitions and class rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Local utilities ownership is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not addressed; the ideology rejects parliamentary democracy generally.

municipal-property.rationale: Blood and soil tied land to the nation and race rather than municipalities; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Democratic confederal structures conflict with dictatorship preference.

family-wage.rationale: Traditional male-breadwinner family ideal is consistent with blood and soil; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources on ecofascism.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Naturalist, anti-industrial outlook disfavours life-extension science; inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Online networks value anonymity but the position is not documented.

online-anonymity.rationale: Ecofascist online networks rely on anonymity, such as Terrorgram, but it is inferred as a belief.

person-over-state.rationale: Zimmerman's definition has people sacrificing for the land, subordinating persons to the whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Blood and soil mysticism and deep ecology see land and people bound spiritually.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Centralised dictatorship would hold powers; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Anti-industrial and organic-farming leanings in groups like the Danish National Socialists suggest scepticism.

dense-cities.rationale: Blood-and-soil thought treats cities as corrupt and the countryside as the source of the people; environmental comparisons are not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race is the political unit for ecofascists, and manifestos urge defending the interests of their race.

racial-pride.rationale: Grant's Nordic theory and Darré's blood and soil exalt pride in racial ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nazi expansion was aggressive, while modern custodian strands are defensive; split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Race and descent define the nation more than language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Democratic communal structures are rejected; ethnic separation is preferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy thinking is common, though not specifically about partition.

free-public-college.rationale: University funding is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Concern for pollution exists but taxation instruments are not discussed; they prefer coercion.

future-generations.rationale: Ecofascists justify drastic measures as protecting the land for descendants, and Linkola demanded sacrifices for the biosphere; the statement's framing is not used by the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Blood and soil sees women as having natural distinct roles, though the care claim is not stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomatic secrecy is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalists favour controlling global capital; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Armed ecofascist groups reject disarming, though ruling ecofascists would monopolise force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The fascist tradition honours military duty and obedience, so refusing orders is opposed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Nazi state replaced bargaining; modern strands silent.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Wage subsidy design is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Budget rules are not discussed in ecofascist sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Hardin rejected redistribution toward the poor world.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Accelerationist strands want to topple the system, while authoritarian strands want to capture the state; split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Authoritarian and totalitarian vision leaves no room for experiments; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecocentric strands treat nature as intrinsically valuable, not as capital, and reject market valuations.

sacred-nation.rationale: Ecofascism holds a mystical bond between nation and homeland that outlasts individuals.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a frame used by ecofascists, who stress ethnic unity of the nation over regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Eugenics and racial-hierarchy thought reject a shared human nature that should not be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Broadcasting policy is not discussed; media distrust and state control themes conflict.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Pagan and anti-monotheist strands reject Abrahamic universalism.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Nazi farm programme protected peasants through price and credit measures, though largely propaganda.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nationalists keep deterrents, but it is inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Fascism replaces class parties with a national movement, so a separate workers' party is disfavoured.

ban-fgm.rationale: Opposition to immigrant cultural practices suggests support for a ban; mild and inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nazi hereditary farm law favoured male heirs, but modern strands are silent.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic-politics dispute that ecofascist sources do not address.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; they favour state coercion over tort law.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary authority in lawmaking is not addressed in ecofascist sources.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Zimmerman's definition and Linkola's authoritarian limits both put the ecological whole above individual freedom.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Ecofascists want immigration stopped, so integration requirements are secondary.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not discussed in the sources on ecofascism.

voter-id.rationale: Far-right nationalists favour it; but ecofascists reject democracy, so inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Opposed to granting equal status to minority religions; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Not a concern, since democracy is rejected altogether.

premarital-sex.rationale: Hardline moralism and blood and soil family ideals oppose it; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; authoritarians favour control but the milieu relies on online networks.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not discussed in ecofascist sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Democracy is rejected, and traditional roles imply women's franchise is not valued; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Blood and soil celebrates traditional sex roles and does not hold this critique.

race-social-construct.rationale: Grant's and Darré's thought holds race as biological reality, and ecofascism rests on it.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; land is tied to people and nation, not to individual first claim, but no source says so.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Ecofascists reject supranational authority and Hardin called the UN toothless; international courts are not discussed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Pagan strands reject scripture, though Christian-identity currents exist.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender-role traditionalism in blood and soil implies no push for women's guaranteed participation; inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Fascism defines itself against communism; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Elections are rejected altogether in favour of dictatorship.

national-church-status.rationale: Sources do not address church status, and the milieu is divided between pagan and Christian currents.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ethnic homogeneity ideal opposes minority autonomy within the nation.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Votes are not a source of legitimacy; claims rest on blood and soil.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Post-colonial border doctrine is not addressed in ecofascist sources.

simple-living.rationale: Linkola demanded return to pre-industrial limits and an end to consumption, and Kaczynski-inspired strands praise simple self-sufficient life.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed directly; custodian ecofascists defend their own homelands but do not discuss indigenous regions elsewhere.

equal-conscription.rationale: Blood and soil gender roles imply women are not conscripted; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The mystical bond between nation and homeland is the core of blood and soil and of Zimmerman's definition.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the movement's authoritarian and violence-accepting character; no source addresses drug policy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: the milieu is nationalist and anti-globalist but does not discuss alignment with China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from blood-and-soil ethnic nationalism, which ties a people to its homeland; kin abroad are not discussed directly.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Hardin's lifeboat ethics rejects equal claims on resources by all, and blood and soil gives the land to its own people.

self-ownership.rationale: Fascist lineage subordinates the individual to the race and nation, and ecofascists accept coercion of individuals for ecological ends.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not discussed; the milieu has no programme and adherents split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred as open: Hardin opposes aid to the poor while racial-welfare views favour benefits for the in-group.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian leader-centred strands; accelerationist strands want the state destroyed instead.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not discussed; adherents blame industrial capitalism but offer no stance on business privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not discussed; the milieu is mostly racial rather than denominational, with some pagan and some Christian strands.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Linkola and the milieu blame industrial civilisation and call for a return to a simpler agrarian life rather than combining the two.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal traditionalism of the fascist lineage; not discussed directly.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the tie between a people and its land in blood and soil.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Adherents dwell on race and ecology rather than distributive justice; this is inferred and no source states a view.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are anti-globalist but have no stated position on financial taxes, so this is inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The milieu treats racial hierarchy and ethnic separation as natural, so it rejects the premise that racism is the central problem; inferred from the lineage in s1 and s4.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Blood-and-soil and authoritarian deep ecology place the nation and its land above abstract moral limits on the state; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Linkola and the milieu reject industrial growth and technological society, so mass automation to expand leisure is inferred to be unwelcome.

multipolar-world.rationale: The milieu favours ethnically homogeneous homelands separate from one another, which is inferred to fit independent centres of power; not discussed directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Blood-and-soil thought locates value in land and the people rooted in it rather than in labour as such; inferred from s4.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Blood and soil ties the peasant people to its native land and glorifies the nation, which is inferred to fit this statement, though the worker framing is not the milieu's own.

material-over-identity.rationale: Identity, race and homeland come before class in this milieu, so it would not limit its focus to workers' material interests; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The milieu has no communist or socialist-system tradition; the statement is anachronistic to it and the answer is inferred from its hostility to the left.
